panels.title: Reachable Nodes
panels.description: Number of registered nodes whose Coordinator heartbeat is currently reachable. Adds the 0/1 reachability values; registered but unreachable nodes contribute zero.

panels.title: Schedulable Nodes
panels.description: Sum of current scheduler-admission flags. A reachable node can be administratively blocked or lack an eligible runtime; reachability and admission are different.

panels.title: Queued Requests
panels.description: Current requests waiting in the Coordinator scheduling queue; excludes requests already assigned to a node.
Allocated resources divided by capacity on schedulable nodes. Nodes with admission disabled are excluded. This is not actual utilization.

panels.title: Running and Paused Environments over Time
panels.description: Coordinator inventory counts evaluated at each historical time step. This is concurrent inventory over time, not the number created during the range.

panels.title: Running and Paused Environments by Node
panels.description: Current Coordinator inventory, one row per registered node and one column per state. Values count logical Environments, not CPU or processes. Zero means none in that state. Historical unreachable registrations can have zero counts. This is an instant snapshot; the dashboard time range does not turn it into a historical total.

panels.title: Average Running Environments per Node
panels.description: Current running inventory divided by currently reachable nodes, including reachable nodes with zero running Environments. No reachable nodes means no meaningful average.

panels.title: Node Status, Scheduling Capacity and Allocation
panels.description: One row per environment and node: heartbeat reachability, scheduler admission, resource sampling, and CPU, memory and disk scheduling capacity. Unknown means missing observations. Sampling uses node_id, with k8s_node_name as a Kubernetes fallback. Samples older than 45 seconds are unknown (15-second scrape interval). Capacity is zero when admission is disabled. Disk capacity is a scheduling value, not physical filesystem size. CPU, memory and disk allocation bars show reserved / underlying capacity on reachable nodes, including starting and running environments. The underlying capacity is retained when admission is disabled, so existing allocations remain visible even when the scheduling capacity columns are zero. These are allocation ratios, not measured utilization. Zero or missing capacity produces Unknown. Bars use a fixed 0–100% scale; values above 100% remain visible as percentages. Colors: green below 70%, yellow at 70–90%, red at or above 90%. Rows are durable registrations, not the current Kubernetes Node list: a removed host can remain Unreachable until its registration is retired. Missing sampling is Unknown, not a reason by itself to declare the host unavailable.

panels.title: Exported and Failed Spans
panels.description: Native Coordinator and adxlet span export counters. Query Ingress traces directly in Tempo.

panels.title: Paused Environments
panels.description: Committed Paused state. Resource samples from before pause are not current usage.

panels.title: Created QPS (1m window)
panels.description: First durably committed Running result for a new Environment. Replays, resume and restart are excluded.

panels.title: Created Peak QPS (1m window)
panels.description: Maximum cluster-wide one-minute average over the selected time range.

panels.title: Created Throughput
panels.description: Successful new creations per second over a window covering the query step. Wide time ranges average bursts instead of leaving gaps between one-minute samples.

panels.title: Create Call Outcomes
panels.description: Application calls, including replay responses. Unknown and cancelled do not imply creation failure.

panels.title: Create Calls in Flight
panels.description: Create calls currently awaiting their final result, including asynchronous SSE work after response headers were sent.

panels.title: Create Call Duration P95/P99
panels.description: Application execution through its final result, including SSE background creation. Replays are included.

panels.title: Environment CPU Usage
panels.description: Sampled running-runtime usage. Samples older than 45 seconds do not contribute current memory. CPU is a monotonic sampled lifetime total; inspect freshness alongside its rate.

panels.title: Environment Memory Usage
panels.description: Sampled running-runtime usage. Samples older than 45 seconds do not contribute current memory. CPU is a monotonic sampled lifetime total; inspect freshness alongside its rate.

panels.title: Fresh and Stale Resource Samples
panels.description: Sampled running-runtime usage. Samples older than 45 seconds do not contribute current memory. CPU is a monotonic sampled lifetime total; inspect freshness alongside its rate.

panels.title: Runtime Logs (selected range)
panels.description: Runtime stdout/stderr line count over the selected dashboard range. No entries can mean idle workloads; check Collector health before interpreting missing data.

panels.title: Control Warnings / Errors (last 5m)
panels.description: Count of WARN/ERROR control log entries emitted during the last five minutes, not alert-rule firings or distinct incidents. A single reconciliation problem can emit both per-Environment and per-node warnings every report interval. Use the repeated-warning table to identify affected nodes, Environment IDs and error causes.

panels.title: Collector Queue Utilization
panels.description: Queued export batches divided by queue capacity, grouped by exporter. Empty/zero queues are normal; missing exporters are not fabricated as zero.

panels.title: Collector Refused / Enqueue Failed
panels.description: Receiver refusals and exporter enqueue failures per second, split by logs/metrics/traces. Each counter is evaluated separately to avoid equal-labelset collisions after rate removes metric names. These are telemetry pipeline failures, not application errors. Some counters are not exposed until used; missing series are not fabricated as healthy zeros.

panels.title: Repeated Control Warnings / Errors (last 5m)
panels.description: Groups repeated WARN/ERROR log entries by node, Environment and error. An empty Environment ID denotes a node-level summary. The count is log lines in five minutes, so the same underlying failure may appear in both an Environment row and a node-summary row.
